Subject: Production errors and latency spike — CareWave (prod)

Hi Redwood support,

We started seeing a spike in latency and 429/500 responses to model requests from our production cluster around 09:10 PST. Traffic profile did not materially change on our side — same request volume but a huge increase in per-request latency (200ms -> 2.5s) and ~18% 429s across the gateway. This has affected patient-facing flows (appointment confirmation).

Attached are a small set of request traces and a screenshot of a 429 from our UI. Can you confirm whether this is on your rate-limiting/burst side or something in the routing layer? Need immediate mitigation — this is impacting live users.

Request logs attached: carewave-logs-20251118.tar.gz

Thanks,
Jen Park
Product Ops | CareWave Health

On Mon, Nov 18, 2025 at 09:22 AM PST, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks — Jen sent this; escalating to SRE/Serving and CS. Short summary: CareWave seeing large latency increase and ~18% 429 rate beginning ~09:10 PST...

Triage notes (quick):
- Observed burst enforcement on tenant tenant_id=carewave-prod at 09:09:58 PST. Token-bucket window currently configured with a 1s burst smoothing window (intended for low-latency guards).
- CareWave’s request profile uses many short, concurrent requests that used to be amortized by our 60s prefix/KV cache; after yesterday's runtime patch the cache sharding changed (minor rollout) and effective per-connection burst saw a 10x spike in instantaneous tokens consumed.
- The combination (smaller burst_window + changed caching behavior) caused the token bucket to rapidly exhaust, triggering 429s and client retries -> cascading latency increases and occasional 500s from queue timeouts.

Proposed mitigations (hot):
1) Immediate (minutes): enable a per-tenant override to increase burst_window to 60s and raise burst capacity by 3x for tenant_id=carewave-prod. This is a low-risk config flip and reversible.
2) Near-term (hours): revert the rollout that changed cache sharding for serving runtime for affected shards (rollback to last known good).
3) Postmortem actions: add automated rollout canary for cache-shard changes gated by synthetic workload approximating CareWave traffic; add a smoother default burst_window for high-concurrency tenants.

I can push the override now but need approval from ops lead + CS to communicate. Also attaching current runtime rate policy snapshot for trace: rate_policy_snapshot-20251118.yaml

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Stef / Marcus / Marissa — looping in CareWave contact (Jen) for transparency. Short summary and asks: 

What happened: a recent runtime change to cache sharding + conservative burst_window (1s) caused instantaneous token exhaustion for CareWave’s concurrent short-request pattern. This resulted in elevated latency and ~18% 429s for ~35m.
Impact: customer production user flows affected (appointment confirmations); potential churn risk if not remediated quickly.
Immediate ask (approval): temporary per-tenant override to increase burst_window to 60s and 3x burst capacity for carewave-prod. Estimated risk: low; change reversible.
Communications: Marissa/Sales will send customer note; Neha will offer a short SLA credit if needed.
Timeline: Marcus can flip override now; recommend flip within 15 minutes.

Jen — we will perform the temporary change and follow up with rollback plan and root-cause postmortem. Apologies for the disruption.
